concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed subcorneal and subepidermal edema and a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa, consistent with neutrophilic panniculitis.
The patient has a history of sickle cell disease and presented with severe intermittent abdominal pain, which is a common symptom of a sickle cell crisis.
The patient has a history of ulcerative colitis and presented with bloody stools, which is a common symptom of an ulcerative colitis flare.
The patient has a history of autoimmune hepatitis and presented with elevated C-reactive protein levels, which is a common symptom of an autoimmune hepatitis flare.
The patient presented with a tender, swollen knee and leukocytosis, which are common symptoms of septic arthritis.
The patient's skin biopsy showed subcorneal and subepidermal edema and a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa, which is consistent with vasculitis.
The patient presented with clusters of hemorrhagic vesicles on her palms, knees, and soles, which is a common symptom of pyoderma gangrenosum.
The patient presented with tender, swollen skin lesions, which is a common symptom of erythema nodosum.
